passages.text: The process has some inherent liabilities however: inadequate stereoselectivity requires a crystallization step, and high-pressure hydrogenation (at 250 psi) requires expensive, specialized manufacturing equipment, and a rhodium catalyst.
The evolved transaminase had a compounded improvement in biocatalytic activity of over 25,000-fold, with no detectable amounts of the undesired, S-enantiomer of sitagliptin being formed.

The benefits of the new process include a 56 percent improvement in productivity with the existing equipment, a 10–13 percent overall increase in yield, and a 19 percent reduction in overall waste generation.
During 2009, Merck scaled up the new process to pilot scale. Plans to commercialize this technology are moving forward.

Merck's tests of available transaminases failed to identify an enzyme with any detectable activity on the sitagliptin ketone. Starting from an R-selective transaminase with some slight activity on a smaller, truncated methyl ketone analog of the sitagliptin ketone, Codexis evolved a biocatalyst to enable a new manufacturing process to supplant the hydrogenation route.

passages.text: The streamlined, enzymatic process eliminates the high-pressure hydrogenation, all metals (rhodium and iron), and the wasteful chiral purification step.

sources.title: Codexis and Merck Amend and Extend Supply Agreement for Enzyme Used in Manufacture of Sitagliptin
qualifications: Company announcement establishes its reported commercial supply history and agreement terms, not an independent audit of process performance or proof of uninterrupted current supply or renewal.
sources.accessNote: Prepared from the source body already read in the immediately preceding editorial turn. accessedAt records this reuse snapshot, not a new fetch. See the prior pilot correction record and origin manifest.

passages.text: Codexis announced the amendment and extension of its agreement with Merck to license and supply a proprietary enzyme used in the manufacturing process for sitagliptin. In 2012 Codexis and Merck entered into a supply agreement for the enzyme and in 2015 signed a multi-year extension, which was to expire in February 2022. This subsequent extension and amendment is for the license and supply of the proprietary enzyme through December 31, 2026. The extension can be renewed for an additional 5 years upon mutual agreement by both companies.
